transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um, I came in because I've been having this issue with eating. It's just... once I start eating, it feels like I disappear and something else takes over. Even while I'm in my own head telling myself to stop, I just keep going until I literally can't stand it anymore.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?

Yeah, I do. Um, after I eat like that, I usually end up going to a bathroom in my dorm, or sometimes I'll find a quiet floor in the library. I just... I make myself throw up. I get really terrified that all that food is just sitting in my stomach and turning into weight, so I have to get it out.
When this happens, do you eat what most people would consider a very large amount of food?

Yeah, definitely. Um, there have been nights after studying where I'll eat at the dining hall, and then I go straight back to my room and just keep eating. I'll have burgers, bowls of cereal, peanut butter, random snacks... really just whatever I can get my hands on. It's way, way more than a normal dinner. I basically don't stop until my trash can is full of wrappers and I physically feel sick.
How often do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen?

Um, for most of this semester, it's been happening several times a week. It's definitely not just a once-in-a-while thing. If I look back over at least the last few months... yeah, there really hasn't been a single week where the cycle stopped.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself?

It affects pretty much everything. I can be having a perfectly decent day in my classes, but if I happen to catch my reflection in a dorm window and I think my stomach or my face looks bigger than the other guys around me... it just ruins it. It makes me feel like I've failed at everything, and I honestly just don't want anyone to even see me after that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent objectively large binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by self-induced vomiting due to fear of weight gain. These behaviors have occurred several times per week for at least the last few months, with marked overvaluation of body shape/weight in self-evaluation. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent episodes of eating a very large amount of food
Loss of control during eating episodes, describing inability to stop even while wanting to stop
Continues eating until physically uncomfortable or sick
Vomiting is driven by fear that food will cause weight gain
Body shape and weight affect self-worth 'pretty much everything'
Perceived appearance changes can ruin the day and trigger feelings of failure
Avoidance of being seen by others when feeling bigger
